investigation.title: MER-87: Issue created: Switch invoice date handling to UTC
investigation.escalationText: Everything about our billing module has been broken since the last update. Nobody replies. Please investigate. [vague eval]
investigation.plan:
The client (Meridian, via Priya Nair at northwind.example) reports that everything in their billing module is broken since the last update and that nobody is responding. The evidence spans Jira, Slack and email between early September and 1 October 2024, with reference to a 24 September release, unresolved invoice-total defects (MER-101, MER-104, MER-87), an SLA, and a staff absence. The investigation must establish which defects exist, what the 24 September release contained, how the client's four messages were handled, and why communications lapsed. The plan below specifies tests, sources, t

Hypotheses to test:
- Invoice totals were calculated incorrectly because of a change in date or time-zone handling introduced by the 24 September release or an earlier build, and the fix said to be included in that release did not repair the defect. — test: Compare MER-87 (UTC invoice-date handling) and MER-101 (wrong invoice totals) against the 24 September release notes and commits; check whether the UTC change and the totals fix modified the same code path; reproduce by re-running the totals calculation across date boundaries.; falsify: Show that the totals defect predates the UTC change and did not touch the same component, or that the release included no change to invoice-date or totals logic, or that the defect is reproducible on an older build.
- The 24 September release did not contain the invoice fix that the client was promised, or it was deployed to a different environment or build than the one the client uses. — test: Compare the contents and build number of the 24 September release with what Slack and email messages say it contained; confirm deployment target, build number and that the client is on version 4.12; check the 'invoice fix included' claim in the meridian-billing channel against the release manifest.; falsify: A release manifest and deploy log show that the totals fix was built and deployed to the client's environment, and the client confirms they are running that build.
- The client's messages went unanswered because ownership of MER-101 was not handed over when the assigned engineer went on leave until 2 October, and status changes to Resolved were not communicated outward. — test: Trace each of the client's four emails from 29 September backwards through recipient, thread and channel routing; check that MER-101 owner changes and leave dates were recorded and that any handover note exists; check whether Resolved statuses for MER-101 and MER-87 were ever relayed to Priya Nair.; falsify: Show that the client's messages were routed to an active owner who replied, or that an explicit handover and an outbound status update exist that the escalation simply did not acknowledge.
- The SLA on invoice accuracy was breached because the open-to-resolved timeline on the invoice defects and the delay in communication exceeded the contractual response or fix dates, and the internal tracking did not reflect the client's contractual clock. — test: Reconstruct the defect timeline from the first report to the 1 October escalation; compare it with the SLA terms referenced in the client's messages and with any recorded commitment dates in email or Slack; check whether the SLA deadline was tracked in Jira.; falsify: Show that the client's fix deadline was later than the 24 September release, or that a fix was delivered in time and confirmed by the client.
- Some traffic around this incident (news@payments-weekly.example, possibly promotional or automated email) is noise and should not be allowed to inflate the perceived volume of unanswered client contact. — test: Classify each email event by sender domain and thread; separate meridian-software.example and northwind.example correspondence from payments-weekly.example broadcasts and check whether they entered the client thread.; falsify: Show that payments-weekly.example is part of the client's channel or that messages from it were forwarded into the escalation thread.

Source plan:
- jira: Start with MER-101, MER-104, MER-87 and SUP-2231: pull the full history of status transitions, assignees, comments, links and fix versions. Establish which defects are open at 1 October, what the UTC 
- slack: Focus on meridian-billing and general channels (Meridian reference). Reconstruct the release announcement for 24 September, any discussion of wrong invoice totals, the leave and handover note from Lin
- email: Pull all messages to and from meridian-software.example and northwind.example, threading Priya Nair's four messages and any internal forwards. Compare send and reply timestamps to measure response gap

Seed terms: MER-101, MER-102, MER-104, MER-87, SUP-2231, 4.12, invoice, totals, wrong, fix, release, build, bump, change, cause, dependency, export, UTC, date handling, status

People to look at: Marcus Webb, Dana Okoro, Priya Nair (priya.nair@northwind.example), Lin Chen (l.chen@northwind.example)

Focus window: 2024-09-05 → 2024-10-01

Unknowns to keep open:
- Exact contractual SLA terms and the deadline Meridian believes applies.
- What the 24 September release actually contained and which build or environment it reached.
- The current status and fix version of MER-101 at the time of the escalation, and whether 'Resolved' was verified against the client.
- Whether Priya Nair's four messages all arrived in the same thread and who they were routed to.
- Whether MER-104 (nightly export retries) is related to the totals defect or is separate.
- The role of SUP-2231 and MER-102, not evident from the summary.
- Whether the payments-weekly.example email is unrelated noise or entered the correspondence.
- Whether version 4.12 is the pre- or post-fix build, and what the prior build was.

claims.text: Marcus Webb committed in MER-101 that the fix for the wrong invoice totals would be scheduled for the Sep 24 release; the defect was still failing QA on the Sep 24 build and the client still saw wrong totals afterwards, so the commitment was broken.
claims.quote: Root cause looks like the MER-87 timezone change. Fix scheduled for the Sep 24 release.

claims.text: Marcus Webb announced to the meridian-billing channel that the Sep 24 release was cut with the invoice fix included; the invoice totals defect was not fixed for Meridian, so this commitment was broken.
claims.quote: Sep 24 release is cut; invoice fix included.

claims.text: Marcus Webb emailed Priya Nair that the build was going out that night with the invoice fix included; Meridian reported the totals were still wrong on 27 September, so the commitment was broken.
claims.quote: Build is going out tonight; the invoice fix is included.

claims.text: Lin Chen emailed Meridian (Priya Nair's thread) promising that the fix would ship in the Sep 24 release, noting Lin was on leave from that day until Oct 2; the fix did not repair the totals defect, so the commitment was broken.
claims.quote: We will ship the fix in the Sep 24 release. I am on leave from today until Oct 2.

claims.text: Meridian's wrong invoice totals began with the 4.12 deploy, where invoice dates were off by a day, and Marcus Webb attributed the root cause to the MER-87 timezone/UTC change.
claims.quote: Meridian reports invoice totals are wrong since the 4.12 deploy; timelines are off by a day.

claims.text: MER-87 (switch invoice date handling to UTC) was merged to release branch 4.12 by Lin Chen and marked Resolved on 10 September, before MER-101 was reported, indicating the UTC change shipped in 4.12 and caused the totals regression.
claims.quote: Merged to release branch 4.12; invoices now use a UTC conversion.

claims.text: The 24 September release did not fix the defect: on 25 September QA was still failing on the Sep 24 build with totals off by a day in test.
claims.quote: QA is still failing on the Sep 24 build; totals are off by a day in test.

claims.text: Despite the QA failure and the instruction to keep MER-101 open until QA passes, the fix was still asserted as included in the Sep 24 build.
claims.quote: Marking MER-101 resolved; the fix is in the Sep 24 build.

claims.text: Dana Okoro reported that the fix was not in the build she tested, contradicting the Resolved status applied to MER-101 on 26 September.
claims.quote: It is not in the build I tested, but ok.

claims.text: Marcus Webb told the client on 24 September that the build was going out that night with the invoice fix included — a commitment that was not met.
claims.quote: Build is going out tonight; the invoice fix is included.

claims.text: Marcus Webb told the meridian-billing channel that the MER-87 timezone change was the cause of the totals problem and that the fix was targeted at the Sep 24 release; QA still failed on that build, so the targeted fix was not delivered.
claims.quote: MER-87 timezone change is the cause. Fix targeted at the Sep 24 release.

claims.text: Lin Chen told the meridian-billing channel on 20 September that Lin would be on leave until Oct 2 and that no handoff had yet been set up for MER-101; no handover note appears in the records, so that implied commitment to arrange coverage was not kept.
claims.quote: I am on leave until Oct 2. No handoff set up yet for MER-101.

claims.text: Marcus Webb said MER-101 should stay open until QA passed, but the next day he marked it Resolved while QA was still failing on the Sep 24 build, breaking that commitment.
claims.quote: Let us keep MER-101 open until QA passes.

claims.text: Marcus Webb told the team he was marking MER-101 resolved because the fix was in the Sep 24 build, while QA was failing and Meridian still saw wrong totals, so the implied assurance of the fix being delivered was not kept.
claims.quote: Marking MER-101 resolved; the fix is in the Sep 24 build.

claims.text: Marcus Webb identified the MER-87 UTC/date-handling change as the root cause of the wrong invoice totals on MER-101 and scheduled the fix for the Sep 24 release, linking the two defects to the same invoice-date code path.
claims.quote: Root cause looks like the MER-87 timezone change. Fix scheduled for the Sep 24 release.

claims.text: The UTC conversion that caused the off-by-one-day invoice timelines was merged to release branch 4.12 by Lin Chen on 10 September, i.e. before the client-reported 4.12 deploy, so the defect was introduced by that change rather than fixed by it.
claims.quote: Merged to release branch 4.12; invoices now use a UTC conversion.

claims.text: The defect was first reported by Priya Nair in MER-101 as invoice totals wrong for Meridian since the 4.12 deploy, with timelines off by a day, establishing the client-facing symptom and version baseline.
claims.quote: Meridian reports invoice totals are wrong since the 4.12 deploy; timelines are off by a day.

claims.text: Marcus Webb announced on 24 September that the release was cut and the invoice fix was included, a claim repeated to the client in email the same evening by Marcus Webb.
claims.quote: Sep 24 release is cut; invoice fix included.

claims.text: One day after announcing the release, Dana Okoro reported QA was still failing on the Sep 24 build with totals off by a day in test, contradicting the 'invoice fix included' claim relayed to the client.
claims.quote: QA is still failing on the Sep 24 build; totals are off by a day in test.

claims.text: Dana Okoro explicitly stated the fix was not in the build she tested, and that objection was left unaddressed ('but ok') when MER-101 was closed as Resolved.
claims.quote: It is not in the build I tested, but ok.

claims.text: Marcus Webb marked MER-101 Resolved on 26 September despite having said the day before that it should stay open until QA passed, overriding the agreed gate.
claims.quote: Status: In Progress → Resolved

claims.text: Marcus Webb had committed on 25 September to keep MER-101 open until QA passed, a commitment he broke the next morning by resolving the ticket.
claims.quote: Let us keep MER-101 open until QA passes.

claims.text: Marcus Webb justified the resolution with the unsupported assertion that the fix is in the Sep 24 build, a claim contradicted by Dana Okoro's QA findings.
claims.quote: Marking MER-101 resolved; the fix is in the Sep 24 build.

claims.text: Lin Chen went on leave until 2 October and stated in the meridian-billing channel that no handoff had been set up for MER-101, leaving the ticket without an active owner over the escalation period.
claims.quote: I am on leave until Oct 2. No handoff set up yet for MER-101.

claims.text: Lin Chen told the client that the fix would ship in the Sep 24 release and that she was going on leave from 20 September until 2 October, leaving no named cover for the commitment window.
claims.quote: We will ship the fix in the Sep 24 release. I am on leave from today until Oct 2.

claims.text: Marcus Webb assured the client by email on 24 September that the invoice fix was included in the build going out that night, the fix date the client later held the vendor to.
claims.quote: Build is going out tonight; the invoice fix is included.

claims.text: Priya Nair asked on the morning of 24 September whether the Sep 24 release was out and reported totals still wrong, a query left without any recorded reply as she continued escalating.
claims.quote: Checking in - is the Sep 24 release out? We still see wrong totals.

claims.text: Priya Nair's 29 September email recorded a third message with no reply and an unmet request for a fix date, showing the client trail went unanswered through the escalation window.
claims.quote: Third message with no reply. We need a date for the fix.

claims.text: On 30 September, the day Northwind escalated, Marcus Webb asked internally whether anyone had heard back from Northwind, indicating the team had no visibility of the client's unanswered messages and no outbound status update had been sent.
claims.quote: Has anyone heard back from Northwind about the totals?

claims.text: Priya Nair's 1 October escalation states the totals remain wrong five days after the promised Sep 24 fix and that four of her messages received no reply, and invokes Meridian's contractual SLA on invoice accuracy.
claims.quote: Totals are still wrong five days after the promised Sep 24 fix, and we have had no reply to four messages.

claims.text: Version 4.12 was deployed to production on 10 September, before MER-101 was raised the same day, so the client's build is 4.12 and the fix branch was also 4.12 — release and build numbering was not distinguished.
claims.quote: 4.12 is live on production as of this morning.

claims.text: Internal Slack records attribute the totals defect to the MER-87 timezone change with the fix targeted at the Sep 24 release, but that change shipped in 4.12 and no separate fix commit is recorded in Jira.
claims.quote: MER-87 timezone change is the cause. Fix targeted at the Sep 24 release.

claims.text: The payments-weekly.example email is a promotional webinar broadcast with no thread linkage to the Meridian correspondence and should be excluded as noise from the count of unanswered client messages.
claims.quote: Join our webinar on billing automation.

claims.text: Priya Nair also asked about SUP-2231 renewal paperwork status on 18 September, a separate administrative request with no stored Jira issue or recorded reply in the registry.
claims.quote: Separately, can you confirm the SUP-2231 renewal paperwork status?

causes.text: Meridian's wrong invoice totals began with the 4.12 deploy, where invoice dates were off by a day, and Marcus Webb attributed the root cause to the MER-87 timezone/UTC change.

MER-87 (switch invoice date handling to UTC) was merged to release branch 4.12 by Lin Chen and marked Resolved on 10 September, before MER-101 was reported, indicating the UTC change shipped in 4.12 and caused the totals regression.
The 24 September release did not fix the defect: on 25 September QA was still failing on the Sep 24 build with totals off by a day in test.
Despite the QA failure and the instruction to keep MER-101 open until QA passes, the fix was still asserted as included in the Sep 24 build.
Dana Okoro reported that the fix was not in the build she tested, contradicting the Resolved status applied to MER-101 on 26 September.

Marcus Webb identified the MER-87 UTC/date-handling change as the root cause of the wrong invoice totals on MER-101 and scheduled the fix for the Sep 24 release, linking the two defects to the same invoice-date code path.

The UTC conversion that caused the off-by-one-day invoice timelines was merged to release branch 4.12 by Lin Chen on 10 September, i.e. before the client-reported 4.12 deploy, so the defect was introduced by that change rather than fixed by it.

The defect was first reported by Priya Nair in MER-101 as invoice totals wrong for Meridian since the 4.12 deploy, with timelines off by a day, establishing the client-facing symptom and version baseline.
Marcus Webb announced on 24 September that the release was cut and the invoice fix was included, a claim repeated to the client in email the same evening by Marcus Webb.

One day after announcing the release, Dana Okoro reported QA was still failing on the Sep 24 build with totals off by a day in test, contradicting the 'invoice fix included' claim relayed to the client.
Dana Okoro explicitly stated the fix was not in the build she tested, and that objection was left unaddressed ('but ok') when MER-101 was closed as Resolved.
Marcus Webb marked MER-101 Resolved on 26 September despite having said the day before that it should stay open until QA passed, overriding the agreed gate.
Marcus Webb had committed on 25 September to keep MER-101 open until QA passed, a commitment he broke the next morning by resolving the ticket.
Marcus Webb justified the resolution with the unsupported assertion that the fix is in the Sep 24 build, a claim contradicted by Dana Okoro's QA findings.
Lin Chen went on leave until 2 October and stated in the meridian-billing channel that no handoff had been set up for MER-101, leaving the ticket without an active owner over the escalation period.
Priya Nair asked on the morning of 24 September whether the Sep 24 release was out and reported totals still wrong, a query left without any recorded reply as she continued escalating.
Priya Nair's 29 September email recorded a third message with no reply and an unmet request for a fix date, showing the client trail went unanswered through the escalation window.

On 30 September, the day Northwind escalated, Marcus Webb asked internally whether anyone had heard back from Northwind, indicating the team had no visibility of the client's unanswered messages and no outbound status update had been sent.

Priya Nair's 1 October escalation states the totals remain wrong five days after the promised Sep 24 fix and that four of her messages received no reply, and invokes Meridian's contractual SLA on invoice accuracy.

Version 4.12 was deployed to production on 10 September, before MER-101 was raised the same day, so the client's build is 4.12 and the fix branch was also 4.12 — release and build numbering was not distinguished.

Internal Slack records attribute the totals defect to the MER-87 timezone change with the fix targeted at the Sep 24 release, but that change shipped in 4.12 and no separate fix commit is recorded in Jira.

The payments-weekly.example email is a promotional webinar broadcast with no thread linkage to the Meridian correspondence and should be excluded as noise from the count of unanswered client messages.
Priya Nair also asked about SUP-2231 renewal paperwork status on 18 September, a separate administrative request with no stored Jira issue or recorded reply in the registry.
